gv_a_well_in_the_middle.description:
You've stood in Gadgetzan. There's a well in the middle of that city and it's dry and the city is dead, and every goblin in Steamwheedle will tell you the range came down three years ago and tipped the table.

That's true, and it explains nothing. A table doesn't tip and then keep tipping for three years.

Bring me residue off the wisps on the seam. They settle where the draw is strongest, and I want to know whether the draw is still increasing.
gv_a_well_in_the_middle.accept_text: Scrape it into the glass vials, not the tin. Tin takes something out of it.
gv_a_well_in_the_middle.turn_in_text:
It's still increasing. It isn't slowing or settling, it's increasing, in the fourth year.

Whatever took that city's water is still thirsty. That's what I couldn't say last week and can say now.

gv_backed_and_set.description:
The weavers in the dig spin the glass into thread. I've never worked out how, and I'd very much like a length of it, because thread takes a curve and a plate doesn't. Vessa cuts the stone, and I set it.

Bring me spun glass out of the vein and I'll back something of yours properly. Tank kit, mind. There's no point in this on somebody standing at the back.
gv_backed_and_set.accept_text: Bring the thread coiled loose, not wound tight. It remembers the shape you give it.

gv_ci_further_down.description:
Sanna has described the shaft to me three times, and each time she's described it as going down, which is a thing shafts do and not worth saying three times.

She means it goes down past where the water is. Nothing drains below the water table. Something is holding that shaft dry, and I'd like to know what, and I'm not able to go myself.

Sanna says there are things on the way down that hum at the rock. She calls them seam singers. You'll have to get past them.
gv_ci_further_down.accept_text: Listen for where the humming's loudest. That's where they'll be waiting.
gv_ci_further_down.turn_in_text:
You said singing, and I've written down singing, and I want to be clear that I don't know what that means.

Whatever is down there arrived when everything arrived. That's three years, and it's been doing this the whole time under a desert nobody walks.

Go carefully down there. I've spent four years wanting to be right about this, and I find I'd rather you came back.

gv_ci_standing_water.description:
I've been in water my whole life. Harbour water, cave water, the pool out there that nobody else will swim in.

I went to the lip of that chamber, and the water in that chamber is standing up. It isn't a wave and it isn't moving at all. It's standing there, held, like something is holding it, and the lattice goes all the way through it.

I came back. You'll notice I came back.

There are cistern lurkers in that water. Kill them, and look at what they were keeping you from.
gv_ci_standing_water.accept_text: Don't touch the water. I didn't, and that's the only reason I'm here to tell you about it.
gv_ci_standing_water.turn_in_text:
Nine times into that gallery on a lungful, and I thought I'd seen the worst thing down here on about the fourth.

I was nowhere near it.

gv_ci_the_choir.description:
Sanna brought up a shard, and it's been ringing on my bench for a whole day. I've put it in sand, I've put it in water, I've put it in a lead box.

There's something down there that strikes the seam, and the whole seam answers. Crystal doesn't do that on its own. Somebody is playing it.

I'm calling it the Resonance. Find it and stop it.
gv_ci_the_choir.accept_text: Bring me the shard it strikes, if you can find it. I'd like to hear what note it plays.
gv_ci_the_choir.turn_in_text:
The one on my bench stopped the moment you came up the spiral, and I didn't need telling what that meant.

I've been cutting this stone for eleven years. I didn't know it could be asked to do anything.

gv_ci_the_siphon.description:
You've found the works. Sanna's description is the first thing anybody has told me in four years that I couldn't have predicted.

Water doesn't rise. I've built an argument on that sentence across five zones and a thousand miles, and I've never once been able to show anybody the thing that breaks it.

Go and break it. Sanna calls it the Siphon.
gv_ci_the_siphon.accept_text: Come back and tell me what it looked like before anything else. I've waited four years to hear it.
gv_ci_the_siphon.turn_in_text:
So it's real.

Four years, and five places. Every one of them was a local problem with a local cause, and every single one of those people was looking at the same machine.

I'd like a moment, if you don't mind. I'll have the rest of it written up by the time you've climbed back down.

gv_ci_the_thirst.description:
Everything in that place is downstream of one room, and I can tell you exactly where it is, because I've been drawing this map for four years without knowing what I was drawing.

Whatever is in there arrived when everything else arrived. It's been drinking a region since, and it hasn't slowed down once, and the fourth year is faster than the third.

I'm not going to tell you to be careful. You've walked the same five places I have. You know what it's cost already.
gv_ci_the_thirst.accept_text: Come back up when it's done. I'd like to see the pool level the next morning with you.
gv_ci_the_thirst.turn_in_text:
It let go.

You came out of the outflow, did you? Everybody does, because there's only the one channel, and it's the channel the water takes. You followed it home.

Oss took the level at dawn, and it's down four inches. Four inches is nothing. Four inches is the first time that number has gone the right way in nine hundred and forty-two days.

gv_does_not_choose.description:
A pool that's filling is a pool with a level. A pool that's being fed has a current, and a current leaves a grain in anything that grows in it.

Get me tideglass off the waterline and cores out of the lattice above it. The crystal grows toward what feeds it. If I'm right, every one of those will point the same way, and the way will be down.
gv_does_not_choose.accept_text: Mark which way each core was facing when you cut it. Without that, they're just pretty stones.
gv_does_not_choose.turn_in_text:
Every single one points down and slightly east, all of them, without exception.

So the water in this pool is only passing through. It goes on its way somewhere and comes back up, and something at the far end of the run is doing the work.

gv_eleven_months.description:
It's been eleven months of paying ninety people's wages out of a hole that's produced nothing, and the ledger in Steamwheedle calls that my fault.

It wasn't my fault. We were four hundred feet down a clean seam when the water came up to meet us, and water doesn't come up, not here, not in a desert.

Go and stand at the mouth. Then come back and tell me whether a man should be closing that or opening it.
gv_eleven_months.accept_text: Don't go past the mouth. I'm asking for an opinion, not a body.
gv_eleven_months.turn_in_text:
You looked a long time, and everybody does.

She'll tell you it was pulled. I've been told a lot of things by a lot of people in three years, and most of them started with the world changing and ended with me owing somebody money.

gv_first_green.description: I brew with the only clean water for a hundred miles, which makes me either the luckiest brewer alive or the one with the shortest supply line, and I haven't decided which. The shelf above the waterline is the only living ground in the region, and it has blindweed on it. Nothing else in Tanaris grows the stuff, and it's what gives my brew its bite. The Shelf Prowlers have had three years of nothing competing with them, and it's made them bold. Go down to the Green Shelf, bring me some of that blindweed, and clear the prowlers off it while you're there.
gv_first_green.accept_text: Pick it with the roots on. It keeps longer, and I'd like to plant a few by the vats.
gv_first_green.turn_in_text: Three years ago this hole had a dozen things living in it. Now it has everything that could find it. The green isn't getting bigger, but the crowd is.

gv_five_places.description:
You came here through the Sands. Before that, Tanaris. Before that the pan, and the Needles, and if you've been at this long enough, the Aspen.

I've walked all five, in that order, starting four years ago, because the thaw was coming early and nobody could tell me why.

Sit down with me. You already know four sixths of this, and nobody has ever put it in front of you in one piece.
gv_five_places.accept_text: Take your time with it. I've had four years to get it straight, and you've got an afternoon.
gv_five_places.turn_in_text:
At every one of those places somebody told me it was a local problem with a local cause. That's five different people, all of them careful, and none of them wrong about their own valley.

It's one problem, and you're standing in it.

gv_four_months_left.description:
Finding the seam was never the problem. The problem is that something has worked out the seam is worth having.

The lattice grows over an exposed face in a season, and once it has, the stone underneath is no good. Whatever it does to the crystal, it does it all the way through. Cut it back and bring me the cores.
gv_four_months_left.accept_text: Bring the cores even if they look ruined. I want to see how far in it gets.
gv_four_months_left.turn_in_text:
These are growing toward the seam. They aren't growing over it, they're growing toward it.

I've been calling it a weed for two years. It's something that wants what I want.

gv_it_is_being_pulled.description:
I've got a figure, a direction and a rate. I've had the first two for a year and the third since this morning, and the third is the one that matters.

The water under this region is being drawn down a shaft four hundred feet below us, by something that started doing it about the time the sky changed.

Take that to Cobble. He won't like it and he won't argue with it. He's better than he looks at keeping those apart.
gv_it_is_being_pulled.accept_text: Let him read it on his own first. He's better with bad news when nobody's watching.
gv_it_is_being_pulled.turn_in_text:
He read it twice and asked one question, which was whether it would stop if somebody made it stop.

I didn't have an answer. I think we're about to get one.

gv_jackals_at_the_lip.description: Nothing on that rim lives off the rim, because there's nothing up there to live off. The Rimfall Jackals are up there because everything that comes out of the hole comes out slowly, and they've had three years to work that out. They've learned where the tired come up, and they sit and wait for them. I've fed half the crews in this camp after that climb, and I know what they look like when they reach the top. Thin the jackals where the road crests at the Dry Rim, north of camp, because that's where they sit.
gv_jackals_at_the_lip.accept_text: Bring the pelts back if they're any good. The nights get colder than you'd think in a hole.
gv_jackals_at_the_lip.turn_in_text: That's much better. A cart gets up that last stretch at walking pace with everyone pushing, and that isn't a moment you want to be fighting.

gv_last_entry.description: You peel the pages apart carefully. It's a ledger, and a proper one, ruled, dated and double-entered, Company accounts from four hundred feet down. The last line is a date and nothing after it. Whoever kept it stopped mid-page and never came back to finish. Tally-Clerk Oss Pinch keeps the camp's books, and she'll know what that date means.
gv_last_entry.accept_text: You close the ledger gently. The pages are still wet, and they tear if you rush them.
gv_last_entry.turn_in_text:
That's Hallick's hand. He kept the face accounts and he went down with the shift.

He balanced it. Look at the bottom of the column. He was four hundred feet under a desert with the water coming up, and he balanced it first.

I'm going to put this in the box with mine.

gv_mv_glassmaw.description:
Forty feet in on a lungful, tie off, forty feet back. That was the job before the gallery dried.

Now I can walk it, and I've walked it, and past the pump chamber the seam opens into rooms made entirely of crystal faces. They're beautiful, and every surface in there will open you up, and one of them moves.

The crews named it Glassmaw. I want it dead.
gv_mv_glassmaw.accept_text: Wrap your hands and your knees before you go in. The floors cut as well as the walls.
gv_mv_glassmaw.turn_in_text:
Nine times I went in on a lungful and I never once got as far as that room.

There's a hole in the floor at the back of it, and it goes down. I looked at it for a long time, and then I came back up here and had a drink.

gv_mv_open_the_door.description:
Nine days, like I said. The first gallery is dry and the dig head is standing open for the first time in a year.

And there are people in it. That's the part I haven't told the Boss yet. They're still on shift, in the sense that nobody ever called the shift, and they don't want anybody down there with them.

They're sodden diggers now. Put them down.
gv_mv_open_the_door.accept_text: Try to look at their faces before you do it. Oss will ask me who they were.
gv_mv_open_the_door.turn_in_text:
There were forty of them. We signed off forty missing and there are forty down there.

Half of them came through with everybody else and took the first wage anybody offered. They weren't from here, and nobody is going to come looking.

I'm going to have to be the one who tells him that, aren't I?

gv_mv_still_on_shift.description:
Each of them carried a brass token with a number on it. You hang it on the board going in and you take it off coming out, and that's how a dig knows who's below.

There are forty tokens still hanging on that board. Bring me what you can off them and I'll take the numbers down properly, which is a thing somebody should have done eleven months ago.

Vein crawlers have got in among them. Kill those as well.
gv_mv_still_on_shift.accept_text: Keep the tokens in the pouch I gave you. Brass rattles, and those galleries carry sound.
gv_mv_still_on_shift.turn_in_text:
I'll do the rest myself, over time.

Hesper Dunn keeps a book like mine out in the port, and she told me once she keeps hers so that in four years nobody can claim the town was always like this. Mine is so that in four years somebody can still say their names.

gv_mv_the_foreman.description: Grebble Vask was my pitboss, and he was the best I ever had. He didn't call the evacuation because calling it cost eleven thousand, and not calling it cost nothing until it cost everything. Pitboss Grebble Vask is still at the head of the gallery in the Mother Vein, still shouting figures. I've heard him from the mouth, and I'd like that to stop. I signed his wages for years, and I'll put my name to this as well.
gv_mv_the_foreman.accept_text: If he's still got his ledger on him, leave it there. I don't want to read his last figures.
gv_mv_the_foreman.turn_in_text:
Thank you for that.

I signed that order. He read it out to me and I signed it, and the thing that's been eating me for a year is that I'd sign it again, because from where I stood on the Tuesday it was the right number.

gv_mv_what_the_pumps.description: Four of those six housings are down there in the sump chamber, and they're mine, and I've wanted them back for a year. There's something in that chamber now, in the place the water left behind. Sanna has seen it from the gallery mouth and she won't go past the arch, and Sanna has gone into that water nine times. The crews call it the Sump. Go down through the Mother Vein to the pump chamber and kill it, so I can get my housings out.
gv_mv_what_the_pumps.accept_text: Take a lamp that won't drown. Sanna's last one went out at the arch.
gv_mv_what_the_pumps.turn_in_text:
You got them out. Look at the face on that casing. The water didn't do that, something sat on it.

I can run four more pumps off these, not that it matters any more. We aren't here for the crystal now, are we?

gv_same_book.description: I've started to suspect a number is only ever worth what the person reading it already believed, which is a terrible thing for a clerk to work out about herself. The Boss and Ulla have both read my book, and both of them say it proves them right. I want the argument stated plainly by both sides, in order, in one afternoon. Go and get it said, him first and her second. Then come back and tell me if I'm wrong.
gv_same_book.accept_text: Don't take sides while they're talking. They'll both try to get you to.
gv_same_book.turn_in_text:
You aren't going to tell me I'm wrong, are you?

Then I'll keep taking it at dawn, and one of them will be right eventually, and my book will have been right the whole time without ever helping anybody.

gv_tell_them_why.description:
There's a man in Steamwheedle who didn't leave Gadgetzan. He was carried out of it on a door by two people whose names he never got, and he's spent three years listening to people say his town had bad luck.

It didn't have bad luck. It had a cause, the cause had a location, and the location is four hundred feet under my feet.

Take him the account. He's owed the sentence, and I'm not able to make the walk any more.
gv_tell_them_why.accept_text: Sit with him while he reads it. He's had enough people walk away from him.
gv_tell_them_why.turn_in_text:
Mazzic reads it twice, slowly, and then puts it down flat on the counter and smooths it with his hand.

I knew it wasn't us. Three years of goblins telling me the desert turned, and I knew it wasn't us.

That doesn't make it better. I want to be honest with you, it doesn't make it better at all. But it's true, and I haven't had one of those about my own town since the day I came out of it on a door.

gv_the_book.description:
Nine hundred and forty-one days of water level, taken at dawn, written down whether anybody wanted it or not.

The Boss says my book proves the flood is seasonal. Ulla says my book proves it isn't. It's the same book.

Take it to her. I'd like to watch somebody else carry it across the camp for once.
gv_the_book.accept_text: Walk slowly with it. Oss will be watching from the door, and she'll enjoy it more that way.
gv_the_book.turn_in_text: She didn't argue with it, and that's the part that worries me. She read it for an hour and then asked what the weather had been doing four days west.

gv_the_book_goes_east.description:
Hesper Dunn out in the port keeps a book like mine. She keeps hers so that in four years nobody can claim the town was always like this.

Mine is nine hundred and forty-two dawns of a number that nobody wanted and that turned out to be the only record anybody had of the thing happening. Copy it and take it to her. A pair of books four days apart are harder to lose than one.
gv_the_book_goes_east.accept_text: Copy it in your best hand. Hesper's a stickler for neatness, and she'll judge me by it.
gv_the_book_goes_east.turn_in_text:
She'll keep it. She'll keep it in the same box and she'll date the box, because that's what we're like.

Somebody in forty years is going to open that and find out exactly when a region stopped drying out. They won't get it from a speech. They'll get it from two clerks nobody listened to.

gv_the_cutters_stock.description:
There's a single seam in the world that shrugs off a spell, and you're standing in the hole it came out of. Before you ask, it wasn't here three years ago either. Nobody cut this stone before the change because nobody had found the hole.

I've got about four months of cut stock left. After that I'm a very skilled woman sitting on a rock. Get me rough off the wall. The seams run up the inside and you can't miss them, because they're the only thing down here that glows.

Shardback crawlers nest on the seams. You'll have to clear them before you can cut.
gv_the_cutters_stock.accept_text: Cut along the grain of the glow, not across it, or the rough cracks before it reaches my bench.
gv_the_cutters_stock.turn_in_text: It's rough, but it's the real thing. You can tell because it goes cold when you hold it near anything cast, and nothing else does that.

gv_the_lip.description: You came down the pass from the Sands, so you've already seen what a hole in limestone looks like when the water's gone. Walk north to the Dry Rim, the edge of this one, and look at what it looks like when the water's still there. There's green down there, and four days in any direction from here there's no green at all. Everybody stands on the rim and looks in once before they start down, and I won't have you be the first who didn't. I did it myself the day we pegged this camp, and I stood there longer than I'd like to admit. Come back and tell me what you saw.
gv_the_lip.accept_text: Mind the loose stone at the edge. It looks solid right up until it isn't.
gv_the_lip.turn_in_text:
It stops people. It's stopped every single person who's come over that rim since I've been here, and I've watched a lot of them do it.

The ones who came through with the change stop longest. I think it's because they've got somewhere to compare it to, and the rest of us haven't.

gv_the_long_way_down.description:
There's one road down and it goes round the hole once. Goblins cut it wide enough to turn a cart on, and then spent four years arguing about whether that was worth it.

Walk it to the shore. Don't take the short way. There's no short way, and the people who've gone looking for one are a story I tell at the fire.
gv_the_long_way_down.accept_text: Keep the wall on your right going down. It's the only thing on that road that doesn't move.
gv_the_long_way_down.turn_in_text: That's forty-six feet of cut road, and the air changes about two thirds of the way down. Everyone notices and nobody expects to.

gv_the_marks.description: Oss's book goes back nine hundred and forty-one days. The rock goes back further, and it's been keeping the same record for nothing, with nobody there to write it down. Find me the old waterlines on the Green Shelf, on the west shore and on the east. I want to know what this pool did before anybody was here to have an opinion about it. I've read waterlines on four other shores, and every one of them told me something the people living there didn't want to hear. The Waterline Serpents lie along both shores, so you'll have to clear them to read the rock.
gv_the_marks.accept_text: Look for the pale bands, not the dark ones. The pale ones are where it stood longest.
gv_the_marks.turn_in_text:
It was lower. Three years ago that pool was eleven feet lower than it's been since, and it's come up steadily.

You'll have noticed that number before, three years. Everyone who came across has.

gv_the_other_two_pumps.description: Two of the pumps work, and they aren't the Company's two. I can clear the first gallery in nine days, and I've been able to clear it in nine days for eleven months. What I can't do is cast new housings out of nothing, and the Shardback Crawlers have been eating the iron off the spoil heap faster than I can pick it over. I've run pumps since before most of this crew could walk, and I've never once been short of iron until this hole. Get me the salvaged iron off the heap, and get the crawlers off it.
gv_the_other_two_pumps.accept_text: Bring me the heavy pieces first. Light iron's no good for a housing.
gv_the_other_two_pumps.turn_in_text:
Nine days is all it's ever been. It's nine days and two people saying the same sentence on the same afternoon, and I've had neither for a year.

I built pumps for twenty years before the world changed and I was good at it, and now I'm a man with four broken housings on a rock.

gv_the_seam_is_the_zone.description:
Here's a thing nobody tells newcomers and everybody works out. You can see the seams from the top, because they're the only lit thing in the hole. I see them from the platform every time I take off.

Stand on the rim, pick one, and follow it all the way down. Everybody who works this wall knows their own seam by sight, and that's how you start.

The best one to start with runs down south-west of here, and Vessa can point you at the others.
gv_the_seam_is_the_zone.accept_text: Take your time choosing. Whichever one you pick, you'll be following it for a while.

gv_the_wet_test.description: I need water from the bottom of that pool, and I need it sealed, because the argument I'm about to make rests on how cold it is, and air ruins that in minutes. Bring it from the deep end, where nobody has stirred it. There's a Pool Horror in the deep end that objects, and it's objected to Sanna nine times. I've measured water in five places across a thousand miles, and this is the sample I'll be held to. Kill the horror and bring me the deepwater, sealed.
gv_the_wet_test.accept_text: Seal it under the surface if you can. One bubble of air and the reading's worthless.
gv_the_wet_test.turn_in_text:
It's colder than the pool it came out of. It's four degrees colder, consistently, from the deep end, and the Flats have been saying the water goes east for longer than any of us have been here, since well before the change.

Water doesn't refrigerate itself. That water has come a very long way underground and it's come fast, and I can now say so with a figure attached.

gv_what_climbs_out.description:
We've lost three loads off the top of the road this season, and jackals don't take crates.

They keep a tally. I want to see it, because I'd like to know whether they've been counting our carts or everybody's.

It's the sunbleached stalkers. Kill them at the top of the road and take the tally sticks they carry.
gv_what_climbs_out.accept_text: Bring the sticks back in the order you take them. The notches might line up with my manifests.
gv_what_climbs_out.turn_in_text:
They've been counting everybody's. That's years of notches, and a third of them are older than this camp.

So they were up there before the dig was, waiting on a road that didn't exist yet. That's patience, and I don't like what it says about them.

gv_what_shrugs_off_a_spell.description: I can tell you vein glass shrugs off a spell. I can't tell you why, and neither can anybody in Steamwheedle, and I've stopped pretending that's fine. I want it tested against something that actually casts, not against me waving my hands at it. Take a backed plate up the galleries and let the Vein-Lit Wisps hit it. They're the only thing down here that throws anything worth measuring, so come back and tell me how the plate held.
gv_what_shrugs_off_a_spell.accept_text: Hold the plate square to them. If they hit it on the edge, I learn nothing.
gv_what_shrugs_off_a_spell.turn_in_text:
It doesn't block, and that's what nobody says properly. It takes the shape of the spell and then it won't hold it, the way water won't hold a fist.

So you want it where you're going to be hit, on a breastplate, a shield or greaves, and not on a hat.

gv_who_drove_this.description: You work the marker loose from the rock. It's a surveyor's marker, bent now, but it was driven properly into the second terrace by somebody who knew how. This bench is four days from the nearest road, so somebody did this work down here before the camp arrived, and did it well. A Terrace Basilisk has been sunning itself on the bench beside it, and it doesn't care for company. Ulla Stormhollow, who's been studying where the water went, will want to see this.
gv_who_drove_this.accept_text: You wipe the grit off the marker. Whoever drove it has been gone a long time, but their work is still standing.
gv_who_drove_this.turn_in_text:
That one's mine. I drove it in my third season, before the camp existed.

I've driven forty of those between the Aspen and here and I've never once come back and found one. You've no idea what it's like to be handed proof that you were somewhere.

gv_works_order.description:
She's got a figure. I've hated that woman for eleven months, and she's got a figure, and I can do arithmetic.

So it's nine days of pumping on the first gallery, her two housings and my four, and she gets a man on the face the whole time writing down what we find. I'll sign that. I'm not going to enjoy signing it.

Take it to Thane before I read it again.
gv_works_order.accept_text: If he asks whether I meant it, tell him I signed it in ink.
gv_works_order.turn_in_text:
He signed it. He actually signed it.

That's nine days, then. Tell everybody, and tell the cook first, because he's the one who's had to seat them.
